title: Why do onions make you cry? #shorts
description:
Slicing an onion starts an enzyme reaction that releases a volatile eye irritant. This animation follows that irritant from the cut cells to your eyes.

Sources: Imai et al., Nature (2002), https://www.nature.com/articles/419685a and Løkke et al., Sensors (2012), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3571771/

Narration uses a synthetic voice.

meta.topic: Why do onions make you cry?

scenes.say: Why do onions make you cry?
An enzyme called alliinase starts the reaction the moment your knife breaks the onion cells.
In the intact onion, that enzyme and the sulfur compounds it acts on are kept apart.
Once they mix, alliinase produces an intermediate that a second enzyme turns into the onion’s tear factor.

events.label: A second enzyme makes the irritant

scenes.say: The product is propanethial S oxide. It evaporates from the freshly cut surface.
When the vapor reaches your eyes, it irritates the sensitive surface.
Your eyes respond by releasing tears that help wash the irritant away.
The sting starts with a cut, but your tears are your eyes’ response.
